title: WaterKron and FlipFlop Hessian: Information-Theoretically Grounded Quantization with Kronecker-factored Hessians
abstract: arXiv:2609.14706v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: How should a Kronecker-factored Hessian approximation be chosen for post-training quantization? We address this question through WaterKron, which combines two-sided GPTQ with row- and column-dependent waterfilling scales and entropy coding. We derive its high-rate distortion with respect to the full Hessian using an explicit Kronecker-Hessian mismatch factor $\Phi$. This factor quantifies the asymptotic distortion penalty due to the Kronecker Hessian approximation and provides a criterion for selecting the factors optimally. Minimizing $\Phi$ leads to a Gaussian covariance-fitting problem with classical ``flip-flop'' updates. We thus give a rate-distortion justification for using the resulting FlipFlop Hessian in quantization. We evaluate it empirically, finding that the FlipFlop Hessian consistently improves KL divergence and perplexity over input-only, marginal, and Frobenius-based Hessian choices.

translated_title: WaterKron与FlipFlop Hessian：基于信息论基础、采用Kronecker因子化Hessian的量化方法
translated_abstract: 在训练后量化中，应如何选择Kronecker因子化的Hessian近似？我们通过WaterKron来解答这一问题，该方法将双边GPTQ与依赖于行和列的注水（waterfilling）缩放因子以及熵编码相结合。我们利用一个显式的Kronecker-Hessian失配因子$\Phi$，推导了其相对于完整Hessian的高码率失真。该因子量化了由Kronecker Hessian近似导致的渐近失真惩罚，并提供了最优选择因子的准则。最小化$\Phi$可归结为一个带有经典"flip-flop"更新的高斯协方差拟合问题。由此，我们为在量化中使用所得的FlipFlop Hessian提供了率失真理论依据。我们进行了实证评估，发现FlipFlop Hessian相较于仅基于输入、边缘分布以及基于Frobenius范数的Hessian选择方法，能够在KL散度和困惑度上一致地取得更好的结果。
tldr: 提出WaterKron量化方法与FlipFlop Hessian近似，通过最小化显式的Kronecker-Hessian失配因子，为训练后量化中的Hessian选择提供了信息论（率失真）理论依据，并在KL散度和困惑度上一致优于现有的Hessian选择方法。
en_tdlr: Proposes WaterKron and the FlipFlop Hessian, providing an information-theoretic (rate-distortion) justification for selecting Kronecker-factored Hessian approximations in post-training quantization by minimizing an explicit mismatch factor, consistently outperforming input-only, marginal, and Frobenius-based Hessian choices in KL divergence and perplexity.
